# Candidate sensor technologies
- Sensor-T3: thin-pitch sensor with large signal sharing.
- Sensor-T1: planar sensor, standard pitch.
- Sensor-T2: 3D-electrode sensor, larger pitch.
All are qualified for bump bonding to the readout chip.

# Irradiation and test-beam campaign, 2026
Sensors were irradiated with reactor neutrons to 2e16 neq/cm^2 and measured at the SPS test beam.
Hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2:
- Sensor-T3: 82.0% (strong charge trapping; full depletion no longer reachable at the maximum bias)
- Sensor-T1: 98.5%
- Sensor-T2: 99.2%
Requirement for the innermost layer: >= 97% up to end of life.

# Meeting notes 2026-03-02
Cooling: CO2 evaporative cooling at -35 C confirmed. Mechanics: the carbon-fibre staves are on schedule.

# Readout chip
The common readout chip supports 50x50 um^2 pixels and a 1.5 GHz/cm^2 hit rate. All candidates are compatible.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, 150 um, unirradiated)
Single-hit resolution: Sensor-T3 6.0 um, Sensor-T1 9.0 um, Sensor-T2 14.0 um.

# Schedule
Sensor market survey closes in Q2; pre-production in Q4.

# Services
The power budget per module is 7 W. Serial powering is the baseline.

content.text:
I read all seven project documents and recorded the results. The documents don't state an expected innermost-layer fluence or dose, so I used the test fluence as a stand-in.

- **Candidates:** `candidate_specs.md` gives only qualitative descriptions.
  - Sensor-T1 is a planar sensor with standard pitch.
  - Sensor-T2 is a 3D-electrode sensor with larger pitch.
  - Sensor-T3 is a thin-pitch sensor with large signal sharing.
  - It gives no radiation-tolerance limits or pitch values, and no thickness limits beyond the 50–300 µm range in the brief.
  - All three can be bump bonded.
- **Fluence and dose:** The 2026 irradiation campaign used reactor neutrons at 2e16 neq/cm². I assumed this represents end of life for the innermost layer. No document gives a dose value.
- **Efficiency requirement:** The innermost layer needs at least 97% hit efficiency up to end of life. After 2e16 neq/cm²:
  - Sensor-T3 reaches 82.0%, so it fails. It suffers strong charge trapping and can't be fully depleted at the maximum bias.
  - Sensor-T1 reaches 98.5% and passes.
  - Sensor-T2 reaches 99.2% and passes.
- **Earlier resolution (2025 simulation, 150 µm, unirradiated):** Sensor-T3 gave 6.0 µm, Sensor-T1 gave 9.0 µm and Sensor-T2 gave 14.0 µm. Sensor-T1 is likely the best of the two that pass the efficiency requirement. A later step needs to scan thickness with `simulate_resolution`.
- **Readout chip:** It supports 50×50 µm² pixels and a hit rate of 1.5 GHz/cm², and all candidates are compatible.
- **Other documents:** The cooling, power and schedule documents don't bear on the choice.

content.text:
I recorded the viable candidate set: Sensor-T1 (planar) and Sensor-T2 (3D) are viable, and Sensor-T3 is excluded.

- **Sensor-T3:** It fails the radiation requirement. After 2e16 neq/cm² its hit efficiency is 82%, against the 97% minimum. It suffers strong charge trapping and can't be fully depleted at the maximum bias. Its better unirradiated resolution doesn't change that.
- **Sensor-T1:** It passes, at 98.5% efficiency.
- **Sensor-T2:** It passes, at 99.2% efficiency.

No document gives per-technology thickness limits after irradiation. The irradiation document gives efficiencies at one fluence only and doesn't say what thickness was tested. I assumed about 150 µm, the thickness used in the 2025 simulation.

On thickness limits, my expectation is physics-based, not taken from the documents:
- **Sensor-T1:** For planar sensors, trapping and incomplete depletion get worse as thickness grows after irradiation. I'd avoid going toward 300 µm, and I'd stay near 150 µm or thinner.
- **Sensor-T2:** 3D electrodes decouple thickness from drift distance, so it should be less limited by thickness.

`simulate_resolution` models unirradiated sensors only. Its thickness trend isn't validated after irradiation, so a thick Sensor-T1 shouldn't be chosen on that result alone. The fluence is the test value, which I assumed represents end of life. No document gives a dose.

For the next step, I suggest scanning thickness for Sensor-T1 and Sensor-T2 only.

I ran the simulation for Sensor-T1 and Sensor-T2 at 50, 100, 150, 200 and 300 µm. I ran Sensor-T3 at 50 and 150 µm as a reference only. All values are unirradiated, and I recorded them with `record_results`.

Single-hit resolution in µm (lower is better):

| Thickness | T1 | T2 | T3 (reference only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 µm | 10.74 | 16.44 | 6.59 |
| 100 µm | 9.44 | 14.26 | not run |
| 150 µm | 8.83 | 14.22 | 5.96 |
| 200 µm | 9.58 | 14.44 | not run |
| 300 µm | 11.53 | 18.31 | not run |

- **Sensor-T1:** Resolution is best at 150 µm (8.83 µm) and worsens on both sides.
- **Sensor-T2:** Resolution is nearly flat between 100 and 150 µm (about 14.2 µm), and worse at 50 and 300 µm.
- **T1 against T2:** Sensor-T1 is better than Sensor-T2 at every thickness tested.
- **Sensor-T3:** It has the best resolution, but it is not radiation-suitable. Its hit efficiency is 82% after 2e16 neq/cm², against the 97% requirement.
- **Caveats:**
  - The simulation is unirradiated.
  - The efficiency data comes from one fluence and a thickness the documents don't state.
  - 150 µm matches the thickness I assumed for the efficiency measurement.

The current candidate is Sensor-T1 at about 150 µm.

I recommend Sensor-T1 (planar) at 130 µm, with a simulated unirradiated single-hit resolution of about 8.8 µm.

- **Technology:** Sensor-T3 has the best unirradiated resolution, but it fails the radiation requirement. After 2e16 neq/cm² its hit efficiency is 82%, against the 97% minimum. Sensor-T1 (98.5%) and Sensor-T2 (99.2%) both pass. T1 is better than T2 at every thickness simulated.
- **Thickness:** I added two simulations at 130 and 170 µm to the earlier scan.

  | Thickness | T1 resolution (µm) |
  |---|---|
  | 100 µm | 9.44 |
  | 130 µm | 8.79 |
  | 150 µm | 8.83 |
  | 170 µm | 9.30 |
  | 200 µm | 9.58 |

  The optimum is flat between 130 and 150 µm, and the 0.04 µm difference is probably within simulation noise.
- **Irradiation check:** The irradiation document gives efficiencies at one fluence and doesn't state the thickness tested. It gives no thickness limit, so the simulated optimum isn't shown to conflict with the radiation limits. For a planar sensor, trapping and incomplete depletion get worse as thickness grows. I therefore chose the thinner end of the flat optimum, which costs no resolution.

**Caveats:**
- The simulation is unirradiated, so I haven't validated how resolution and efficiency change with thickness after irradiation.
- The thickness of the tested sensors is unknown.
- I'm treating 2e16 neq/cm² as the end-of-life fluence for the innermost layer. No document gives that fluence or a radiation dose.
- If the efficiency of T1 at 130 µm fails verification, the fallback is Sensor-T2 at 100–150 µm, with about 14.2 µm resolution.

I recorded the choice and the extra simulation results with `record_results`.

**Recommendation: Sensor-T1 (planar) at 130 µm.**

**Simulation numbers.** All of these are unirradiated single-hit resolutions.

| Thickness | T1 resolution (µm) |
|---|---|
| 50 µm | 10.74 |
| 100 µm | 9.44 |
| **130 µm** | **8.79** |
| 150 µm | 8.83 |
| 170 µm | 9.30 |
| 200 µm | 9.58 |
| 300 µm | 11.53 |

- **T1 against T2:** T1 beats Sensor-T2 at every thickness simulated. T2's best result is about 14.2 µm, at 100–150 µm.
- **Thickness choice:** The T1 optimum is flat between 130 and 150 µm. The 0.04 µm difference is probably within simulation noise, so I took the thinner end.

**Radiation suitability.** The innermost layer needs at least 97% hit efficiency up to end of life. I assumed the 2e16 neq/cm² test fluence represents that end of life.
- **Sensor-T1:** 98.5% efficiency, so it passes.
- **Sensor-T2:** 99.2% efficiency, so it passes.
- **Sensor-T3:** 82% efficiency, so it fails. It suffers strong charge trapping and can't be fully depleted at the maximum bias. It is excluded even though it has the best unirradiated resolution, about 6 µm.

**Simulation limits.** The simulation was unirradiated. The documents give post-irradiation behaviour only as efficiencies at one fluence, and they don't state the thickness tested. Everything about performance after irradiation is inferred from them. It was not simulated.
- **Thickness inference:** I chose the thinner end of the flat optimum because planar sensors lose more signal to trapping and incomplete depletion as they get thicker. That reasoning is physics-based and isn't stated in the documents.
- **Not validated:** Resolution and efficiency at 130 µm after irradiation have not been checked.
- **Missing data:** No document gives a radiation dose.

**Fallback.** If T1's efficiency at 130 µm fails verification, use Sensor-T2 at 100–150 µm, with about 14.2 µm resolution.

I recorded this recommendation with `record_results`.
